t: This is the tomb of Flight Sub-Lieutenant Reginald Warneford, on the northern approach to the Great Circle at Brompton Cemetery. Warneford was a British aviator in the Royal Naval Air Service, born in 1891 and killed in 1915. He received the Victoria Cross for air-bombing a Zeppelin during the First World War. That was the first victory of a heavier-than-air aircraft over a lighter-than-air dirigible, which is why he is remembered here.
